title: Hankel matrix of a power series
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let
$C(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in K[[T]]$ be a
formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series], with coefficients $c_n\in K$. The Hankel matrix of $C$ is the infinite
matrix [def-weil-matrix], with rows and columns indexed by $r,s\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$,

$$
\mathcal H(C)=(c_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}.
$$

Its rank (the Hankel rank of $C$) is the supremum, in $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$ [def-weil-extended-natural-supremum], of the ranks over $K$ [def-weil-matrix-rank] of its finite square submatrices [def-weil-submatrix]; it is finite if and only if these ranks are bounded.

mathlib_searches.verdict: no match for the definition as stated: the Hankel matrix is `Matrix.of fun r s : ℕ => PowerSeries.coeff (r + s) C : Matrix ℕ ℕ K`, and `Matrix.eRank` of it is the dimension of its column span, which over a field equals the supremum of the ranks of its finite square submatrices; Mathlib proves only `≤` (eRank_submatrix_le), not the equality, so the node is stated from its notions
